_note: Layer 1 for both sheets, one section per input name (publish_draft.INPUTS): facts about the railroad that the plan graph does not hold. Read with hartlib.layer_files; the schematic-maps plugin reads a section as it read the old <sheet>.plan_overrides.json.

staging._note: Facts about the railroad that the AnyRail plan 5.3c does not hold or holds wrongly. Every output uses them. Since 5.3c (owner, 2026-11-19) the plan draws the Switch 7 crossover, Switches 13, 11 and 9 with EH-1 to EH-3, and no crossover T41/T43, all left-hand as built; the helix comes from the plan, cut at -5 cm (the schematic-maps plugin's schematic anyplan --cut -5 --stubs).

edits._note: Switch numbers, not part numbers. Switches 23, 35 and 7 are crossover or three-way halves that share one number, so a half is named as number@track once a track leaving it has a name, and before that as number@neighbour: the half a track joins to that switch (23@1, 35@23, 23@15, 35@33, 7@33, 7@13; 7@5 would answer both halves of 7). Only the relabel edit above keys by plan part number.

staging._milepost_origin: Switch 1 is MP 5.7 (owner, 2026-11-19): the P&OV met the P&LE at Neville interlocking, about PLE 5.7 (www/library/chartiers-valley-railroads.html). The count runs east in scale miles and carries on through the helix to the main and upper levels.
staging._milepost_route: The count runs the long way round the staging main: Brick-Plane, East Ext, Main East, East Lead, then the two throats into the helix (through the Switch 35 crossover to 39). Main West and West Ext, the west part of the loop, carry none.
staging._stations: West Yard is W-1 and W-2 with Switch 3 (owner, 2026-11-14). Brick is the interlocking between Switches 1 and 3: a control point, not a station.

main_upper._note: Facts about the railroad that the AnyRail plan 5.3c does not hold or holds wrongly. Since 5.3c (owner, 2026-11-19) the plan has the peninsula at 4.25 in (10.8 cm) and the closet junction (223, T331; T300 in 5.3b) on the upper level where it is built, so no height or move edit is needed. Band names, their level numbers and the 5 cm cut are railroad facts kept here (docs/ops/SCHEMATIC_SPEC.md, layer 1).

edits._note: Owner's switch numbers (2026-11-14, renumbered 2026-11-19): main level 101+, upper level 201+, odd only, left to right as drawn on the approved sheet, main line first at the same position, then top to bottom. A crossover takes one number with A and B (A the left half), numbered where its A half stands; the three-way's halves pair with T183 and T194 as crossovers 101 and 103; the helix-top crossovers are main level (127, 131). T15 and T1 (121) and T184 and T14 (125) are one crossover each on the ground (owner, 2026-11-19), so the main level from 121 east was renumbered: 121 and 123 became 121A and 121B, 125 became 123, 127 and 131 became 125A and 125B, 129 became 127, 133 became 129, 135 became 131. The upper level was renumbered by the same rule on the same day: 207 and 209 swapped, the 213 crossover became 211 and 211 became 213, 231 and 233 swapped, 239 became 241, the 241 crossover 243, and 243 became 239. The double crossover is one part (225). Keys are the plan 5.3c part numbers (re-keyed from 5.3b by position, 2026-11-19); the three-way's halves have no part number in the plan, so they are named by their part ids (TO_3W33789-1 and -2).

levels._assign: The level a junction is on, whatever its plan height: 127B and 131B are on the upper level (10.8 cm). A railroad fact, so layer 1 (owner, 2026-11-21; was in preferences.json).

main_upper._helix_side: Fact, not a preference: the helix is at the east end of every level (ADR-022: timetable east runs toward Princess and the helix).
